themes_detail.label: Street Infrastructure Crisis Accelerating
themes_detail.summary: Street condition complaints exploded to 44 this week compared to a 5.5-per-week baseline over the prior 8 weeks—a 700% spike (z-score: 14.82)—signaling rapid deterioration of roads and sidewalks in Morningside Heights/Hamilton Heights that demands immediate city response.
evidence: 44 street condition complaints THIS WEEK vs. 5.5 average weekly baseline (8-week comparison)
700% increase represents highest z-score spike (14.82) in entire dataset
Community board has repeatedly requested DOT capital funding for street infrastructure, suggesting chronic underinvestment
reporting_angles: Inspect specific streets in the district to identify whether spike is localized (e.g., construction damage, winter deterioration) or city-wide neglect
Interview residents about safety risks (trip hazards, wheelchair accessibility) from street conditions

themes_detail.label: Unsanitary Animal Crisis Emerging
themes_detail.summary: Unsanitary animal private property complaints spiked to 3 this week from a 0.1 baseline—a 2300% increase (z-score: 8.69)—indicating a sudden pest or animal management crisis that may signal broader neighborhood sanitation decline.
evidence: 3 unsanitary animal private property complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.1 average weekly baseline
2300% spike with z-score of 8.69 (severe statistical anomaly)
Parallels broader sanitation spike: street sweeping complaints up 967% last week (4 vs 0.4 avg)
reporting_angles: Identify what specific animals (rats, pigeons, etc.) are driving complaints and whether a particular building or area is epicenter
Interview DOHMH and animal control to understand response capacity and whether this reflects city-wide pest pressure or local neglect

themes_detail.label: Noise Complaints Spiked Last Week
themes_detail.summary: Street and sidewalk noise complaints surged to 93 last week compared to an 18.4-per-week baseline—a 406% spike (z-score: 6.97)—suggesting construction, street activity, or outdoor events creating acute livability complaints.
evidence: 93 street/sidewalk noise complaints last week vs. 18.4 average weekly baseline (406% spike, z-score: 6.97)
Residential noise remains endemic at 1,546 complaints over 90 days, but street/sidewalk subset accelerating
Street noise now represents meaningful share of total noise burden alongside ongoing residential issues
reporting_angles: Map which streets or blocks are generating spike—is it tied to specific construction project, street fair, or ongoing commercial activity?
Determine whether NYPD/311 enforcement of noise violations accelerated or declined during spike week

themes_detail.label: Electrical Infrastructure Strain
themes_detail.summary: Electric utility complaints jumped to 36 last week from a 14.5-per-week baseline—a 148% increase (z-score: 4.75)—raising questions about aging electrical infrastructure capacity as demand peaks or weather stresses the grid.
evidence: 36 electric complaints last week vs. 14.5 average weekly baseline (148% increase, z-score: 4.75)
Spike follows heat/hot water complaints (5,773 over 90 days)—suggesting thermal strain or seasonal load stress
Community board budgets consistently request transit and utility infrastructure upgrades, implying acknowledged deficiencies
reporting_angles: Check ConEd outage records and voltage issues in the district to confirm whether surge reflects customer complaints about actual service failures
Interview Con Edison about infrastructure adequacy and whether the aging Morningside/Hamilton Heights grid needs upgrades

themes_detail.label: Damaged Tree Complaints Peaked 2 Weeks Ago
themes_detail.summary: Damaged tree complaints reached 6 two weeks ago compared to a 0.4-per-week baseline—a 1500% spike (z-score: 11.62)—suggesting storm damage, disease, or neglect of the neighborhood's tree canopy.
evidence: 6 damaged tree complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.4 average weekly baseline (1500% spike, z-score: 11.62)
Represents second-highest z-score spike in dataset after street conditions
Community board has requested park/playground reconstruction funding, suggesting deferred tree maintenance
reporting_angles: Determine whether spike was weather-related (windstorm, heavy snow) two weeks prior or signals disease/pest outbreak (e.g., emerald ash borer)
Check NYC Parks tree removal and trimming queue for Morningside/Hamilton Heights to assess if complaints reflect service delays
